name_note: GTDB treats this organism as the species s__Bifidobacterium infantis, while the literature and NCBI call it a subspecies of Bifidobacterium longum.

sentences.text: Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis is a common member of the infant intestinal microbiota, characterised by its foraging capacity for human milk oligosaccharides.

Among the three recognised subspecies of Bifidobacterium longum, subsp. infantis achieves high levels of cell growth on human milk oligosaccharides and is associated with early colonization of the infant gut.
Its genome features gene clusters predicted to bind, cleave and import milk oligosaccharides, and specific beta-galactosidases of the subspecies have been characterised for degrading these sugars.
A study provided Bifidobacterium longum subsp. infantis EVC001 to breastfed infants to test whether the probiotic organism persists in the gut after supplementation ends.
